meanings: to be up to a task

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — historically linked to physical strength and overcoming an opponent
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 胜's reading shèng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
亻 (person) — 任 relates to a person taking on a responsibility or role.
壬 (rén) gives a hint of the sound — 任 is pronounced rèn, a connection that has shifted somewhat.

example.hanzi: 他完全能够胜任这项工作。
example.pinyin: tā wánquán nénggòu shèngrèn zhè xiàng gōngzuò.
example.english: He is fully qualified for this job.
example.fact: NASA's astronaut selection process accepts fewer than 0.2% of applicants, screening tens of thousands of candidates for the small number of positions needed to crew the International Space Station. Even after selection, candidates undergo roughly two years of training before being certified qualified for spaceflight duty.

components.note: 手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 妈妈让我看好弟弟，别让他乱跑。
example.pinyin: māma ràng wǒ kānhǎo dìdi, bié ràng tā luàn pǎo.
example.english: Mom told me to keep an eye on my little brother so he doesn't run off.
example.fact: Lifeguards are trained to scan their assigned zone every ten seconds and reach any swimmer within twenty to thirty seconds, a rule known as the 10/20 principle. Drowning can happen silently in under a minute, without the loud thrashing shown in movies.

meanings: fat (in the body, in a plant, or in food)

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 脂 names a substance in the body, fat.
旨 (zhǐ) gives the sound — an exact match with 脂, differing only in tone.
⺼ (flesh, body) — 肪 is a kind of body fat.
方 (fāng) gives a sound close to fáng, sharing the same sound and differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 橄榄油含有大量对心脏有益的脂肪。
example.pinyin: gǎnlǎnyóu hányǒu dàliàng duì xīnzàng yǒuyì de zhīfáng.
example.english: Olive oil contains a large amount of fat that is good for the heart.
example.fact: Blue whales carry a layer of blubber up to 20 centimeters thick that insulates them in freezing polar waters and stores enough energy to fuel migrations of over 8,000 kilometers without feeding. This fat reserve is central to how the largest animals on Earth survive months between meals.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 副 originally related to cutting a matching secondary copy
畐 (fú) gives the sound — an exact match with 副's reading fù
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.
用 is thought to derive from a picture of a bucket or a wooden fence used in ritual divination; the object being used gave the character its meaning 'to use, to employ.'

example.hanzi: 这种药可能有轻微的副作用。
example.pinyin: zhè zhǒng yào kěnéng yǒu qīngwēi de fùzuòyòng.
example.english: This medicine may have mild side effects.
example.fact: In the late 1950s, the sedative thalidomide was prescribed to pregnant women for morning sickness before its severe side effect — causing birth defects in thousands of infants — was discovered. The disaster led directly to the strict drug-safety testing requirements used worldwide today.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 零 originally described light, scattered rain, extended to mean a fragment or zero.
令 (lìng) is an exact match for the sound of 零, differing only in tone.
钅 (metal) — 钱 relates to money, since early Chinese coins were made of metal
戋 (jiān) gives a loose sound connection to 钱's reading qián

example.hanzi: 我口袋里只有一些零钱。
example.pinyin: wǒ kǒudài lǐ zhǐyǒu yìxiē língqián.
example.english: I only have some small change in my pocket.
example.fact: The U.S. Mint estimates that Americans keep roughly $60 billion worth of coins sitting unused in jars, drawers, and couch cushions rather than in circulation. That much idle change is one reason the Federal Reserve periodically has to order fresh coin production to keep up with demand.

components.note: A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
责 shows 贝 (money, a cowry shell) at its base, tied to a debt that must be repaid — giving 责 its meaning 'duty, responsibility, to blame.'

example.hanzi: 考试没考好，他一直在自责。
example.pinyin: kǎoshì méi kǎohǎo, tā yīzhí zài zìzé.
example.english: He kept blaming himself after doing poorly on the exam.
example.fact: Survivor guilt, first documented among concentration camp survivors and later studied in soldiers and disaster survivors, describes intense self-blame felt by people who lived through an event that others did not — even when they had no ability to change the outcome.

components.note: 凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 她对流浪动物充满同情心。
example.pinyin: tā duì liúlàng dòngwù chōngmǎn tóngqíngxīn.
example.english: She is full of compassion for stray animals.
example.fact: Elephants have been observed standing vigil over the bodies of dead herd members, touching the bones with their trunks and feet for long periods. Researchers cite this behavior as evidence of empathy and grief in a species outside our own.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 运's meaning 'to move, transport,' and by extension 'fortune,' the movement of one's life.
云 (yún) gives a sound hint — 运 is pronounced yùn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
车 (cart) — relates to 转's meaning 'to turn, change direction,' like a wheel turning.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 转 is pronounced zhuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 这台机器一直运转正常。
example.pinyin: zhè tái jīqì yīzhí yùnzhuǎn zhèngcháng.
example.english: This machine has been running normally.
example.fact: The Earth completes one full rotation every 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 seconds — slightly short of 24 hours. That is why a sidereal day, measured against distant stars, runs a few minutes faster than the familiar solar day.

components.note: 彳 (step, to walk) — an older, now faded connection tied to movement.
艮 (gèn) gives a hint of the sound — 很 is pronounced hěn, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.
又 (a hand) — reaching out to try to catch something.
隹 (a bird) — catching a bird by hand is hard, giving 难 its meaning 'difficult.'
讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō

example.hanzi: 这件事最后会怎样，现在很难说。
example.pinyin: zhè jiàn shì zuìhòu huì zěnyàng, xiànzài hěn nán shuō.
example.english: It's hard to say how this will turn out in the end.
example.fact: Meteorologist Edward Lorenz discovered in the 1960s that tiny rounding differences in his weather simulations produced wildly different forecasts, giving rise to chaos theory and the popular 'butterfly effect.' It remains a key reason weather forecasts grow unreliable beyond about ten days.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
戈 (a dagger-axe, a weapon) — 战 relates to fighting and war.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 战 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 两国之间随时可能开战。
example.pinyin: liǎng guó zhījiān suíshí kěnéng kāizhàn.
example.english: War could break out between the two countries at any moment.
example.fact: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 is recorded as history's shortest war, lasting only about 38 minutes between the British Empire and the Sultanate of Zanzibar before the sultan's forces surrendered.

components.note: 穴 (hole/cave) — 窗 originally described an opening for light and air.
囱 (cōng) gives a sound distantly related to chuāng, having drifted apart over time.
穴 depicts a cave or hole, here representing an entrance or opening.
巾 (cloth) hangs at the entrance, forming the picture of a curtain covering an opening.

example.hanzi: 请把窗帘拉上，外面太亮了。
example.pinyin: qǐng bǎ chuānglián lā shàng, wàimiàn tài liàng le.
example.english: Please close the curtains, it's too bright outside.
example.fact: During World War II, Britain's blackout regulations required households to cover every window with heavy curtains or black paper after dark, so that no light could guide enemy bombers to cities. Wardens patrolled the streets at night to enforce compliance.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — relates directly to 切's meaning 'to cut.'
七 (qī) gives a sound hint — 切 is pronounced qiè, sharing the same initial consonant.
廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'

example.hanzi: 医生小心地把伤口切开。
example.pinyin: yīshēng xiǎoxīn de bǎ shāngkǒu qiē kāi.
example.english: The doctor carefully cut the wound open.
example.fact: Before general anesthesia was introduced in the 1840s, surgeons operated on fully conscious patients and valued speed above all. Scottish surgeon Robert Liston was famous for amputating a leg in under 30 seconds to minimize the patient's suffering.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) gives the sound — 视 is also pronounced shì, an exact match.
率 originally depicted a twisted cord or string 幺 being pulled taut in a frame — later extended to meanings like 'to lead' (pulling something along) and 'rate, ratio.'

example.hanzi: 这部剧的收视率一直很高。
example.pinyin: zhè bù jù de shōushìlǜ yīzhí hěn gāo.
example.english: This drama's ratings have consistently been high.
example.fact: Super Bowl LVIII in 2024 drew roughly 123 million U.S. viewers, making it the most-watched television broadcast in American history and surpassing the 1969 Apollo 11 moon landing telecast.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — 苏 relates to certain aromatic plants and to reviving, coming back to life
稣 (sū) gives the sound — 苏 is also pronounced sū, an exact match
王 (jade) — an older semantic link to precious, ornamental materials.
册 (cè) gives a sound distantly related to shān, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 苏珊是我们班新来的老师。
example.pinyin: Sūshān shì wǒmen bān xīn lái de lǎoshī.
example.english: Susan is the new teacher in our class.
example.fact: The name Susan derives from the Hebrew Shoshanna, meaning 'lily' or 'rose,' by way of Greek and Latin forms. It became one of the most popular English given names for girls in the mid-20th century before falling out of fashion by the 1990s.

components.note: 人 (person), doubled — one person shown following another depicts the idea of accompanying or coming from somewhere.
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

example.hanzi: 他从中得到了很多经验。
example.pinyin: tā cóngzhōng dédào le hěn duō jīngyàn.
example.english: He gained a lot of experience from it.
example.fact: After the near-catastrophic Apollo 13 mission in 1970, NASA engineers spent months analyzing exactly what had gone wrong with the oxygen tank. The lessons learned directly shaped safety redesigns used in every subsequent Apollo mission.

components.note: 千 (thousand) — 重 pictures a heavy burden carried a great distance.
里 (a unit of distance, like a mile) — carrying something a thousand 里 emphasizes how heavy and significant a burden it is, giving 重 its meaning 'heavy' or 'important.'
里 (a unit of distance, related to a village measure) — 量 relates to measuring quantity.
旦 (dàn) gives a hint of the sound — 量 is pronounced liàng, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 这个包裹的重量超过了限制。
example.pinyin: zhège bāoguǒ de zhòngliàng chāoguò le xiànzhì.
example.english: This package's weight exceeds the limit.
example.fact: Until 2019, the kilogram was defined by a single platinum-iridium cylinder kept in a vault near Paris. Scientists then redefined it using the Planck constant, so weight standards no longer depend on one physical object that could theoretically be damaged.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 露 names a form of moisture related to weather.
路 (lù) gives the sound — an exact match with 露.
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 他很久没有在公众场合露面了。
example.pinyin: tā hěn jiǔ méiyǒu zài gōngzhòng chǎnghé lòumiàn le.
example.english: He hasn't appeared in public for a long time.
example.fact: Billionaire Howard Hughes spent his final years almost entirely out of public view, reportedly going nearly a decade without being photographed. His disappearance fueled widespread rumors about his health and even his identity.

components.note: 土 (earth) shows 埋 relates to putting something into the ground.
里 (lǐ) gives a sound distantly related to mái, having drifted apart over time.
艹 (grass) — 葬 pictures a burial taking place under the grass.
死 (death, corpse) contributes to the character's form, naming who is being laid to rest.
廾 (two hands) shows the corpse being carefully laid down, completing the picture behind 葬's meaning 'to bury.'

example.hanzi: 古埃及人会把法老埋葬在金字塔里。
example.pinyin: gǔ Āijí rén huì bǎ fǎlǎo máizàng zài jīnzìtǎ lǐ.
example.english: The ancient Egyptians would bury pharaohs inside pyramids.
example.fact: When archaeologist Howard Carter opened Tutankhamun's tomb in 1922, it was one of the only pharaonic burial sites found nearly intact. It contained over 5,000 artifacts, including the pharaoh's iconic solid-gold burial mask.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'
忄 (heart/mind) — the state of mind being described.
夬 (a decisive, resolute action) — a resolute state of mind, giving 快 its meaning 'fast, quick.'

example.hanzi: 政府决定加快这项工程的进度。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ juédìng jiākuài zhè xiàng gōngchéng de jìndù.
example.english: The government decided to speed up the progress of this project.
example.fact: China's Fuxing bullet trains reach a commercial operating speed of 350 km/h, covering the roughly 1,300-kilometer trip from Beijing to Shanghai in under four and a half hours — a journey that once took over 30 hours by conventional rail.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咖 is used in a word for something taken by mouth (coffee).
加 (jiā) gives a sound close to kā, sharing the same rhyme with a different initial.
口 (mouth) — 啡 is used in a word for something taken by mouth (coffee).
非 (fēi) gives the sound — an exact match with 啡.
广 (shelter/building) — 店 names a building used for business.
占 (zhàn) gives a sound distantly related to diàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 我们在咖啡店里聊了一个下午。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zài kāfēidiàn lǐ liáo le yí ge xiàwǔ.
example.english: We chatted in the coffee shop for a whole afternoon.
example.fact: Coffee is believed to have been discovered in Ethiopia, where legend credits a goatherd named Kaldi who noticed his goats becoming unusually energetic after eating berries from a certain tree. The practice of brewing coffee later spread through Yemen and the wider Islamic world by the 15th century.

components.note: 止 (a footprint), shown twice — one foot placed in front of the other, the source of 步's meaning 'step, pace.'
彳 depicts a step with the left foot; together with 亍 (a step with the right foot), 行 shows a person walking or moving.
亍 depicts a step with the right foot, complementing 彳 to form the idea of walking or travel.

example.hanzi: 从这里步行到火车站只要十分钟。
example.pinyin: cóng zhèlǐ bùxíng dào huǒchēzhàn zhǐ yào shí fēnzhōng.
example.english: It only takes ten minutes to walk from here to the train station.
example.fact: The longest unbroken walk on record was completed by George Meegan, who walked roughly 30,000 kilometers from the southern tip of South America to the northern edge of Alaska between 1977 and 1983 — a journey of nearly six and a half years.

components.note: 十 (ten, suggesting abundance) — relates to 华's meaning 'flowery, splendid,' an abundance of blossoms.
化 (huà) gives a sound hint — 华 is pronounced huá, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
丽 is the simplified form of 麗, which depicted the ornate antlers of a deer (鹿) — a fitting image behind its meaning 'beautiful, magnificent.'

example.hanzi: 这座宫殿的装饰非常华丽。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò gōngdiàn de zhuāngshì fēicháng huálì.
example.english: This palace's decoration is extremely gorgeous.
example.fact: The Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles contains 357 mirrors and took roughly six years to complete in the late 17th century. It later became the site where the treaty ending World War I was signed, in 1919.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 常 originally referred to a long skirt or banner made of cloth, later coming to mean something 'usual' or 'ordinary.'
尚 (shàng) gives a hint of the sound — 常 is pronounced cháng, a connection that has drifted over time.
冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'

example.hanzi: 感冒是一种很常见的疾病。
example.pinyin: gǎnmào shì yì zhǒng hěn chángjiàn de jíbìng.
example.english: The common cold is a very common illness.
example.fact: More than 200 different virus strains, most commonly rhinoviruses, can cause the common cold. That genetic diversity is one reason a single universal vaccine against it has never been developed despite decades of research.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 烧 describes burning or cooking with fire.
尧 (yáo) gives a rhyme close to shāo, with a different initial.
亻 (person) — 伤 describes physical harm done to a person.
The remaining strokes are a simplified trace of 伤's traditional phonetic component, which is close in sound to shāng.

example.hanzi: 他在事故中受到了严重的烧伤。
example.pinyin: tā zài shìgù zhōng shòudào le yánzhòng de shāoshāng.
example.english: He suffered severe burns in the accident.
example.fact: Surgeons have used skin grafts to treat severe burns since at least the 19th century. Modern burn units can now grow sheets of a patient's own skin cells in a lab from a postage-stamp-sized sample within about two to three weeks for grafting onto large wounds.

meanings: You are welcome to do whatever you like!

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 请's meaning 'to request, invite; please,' a spoken request.
青 (qīng) gives a sound hint — 请 is pronounced qǐng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
亻 (person) — 便 relates to what is convenient or comfortable for a person.
更, read as biàn in this context, matches the sound of 便 exactly, though the same component is read gèng ('more') in other words.

example.hanzi: 如果你想先走，请便。
example.pinyin: rúguǒ nǐ xiǎng xiān zǒu, qǐng biàn.
example.english: If you want to leave first, please go ahead.
example.fact: The economic term laissez-faire, French for 'let (them) do,' originated in 18th-century France when physiocrat economists argued that government should let markets operate without interference — a principle later cited by economists from Adam Smith onward.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — held in a hand, the image behind 布's meaning 'cloth' and, by extension, 'to spread out, distribute.'
The character traces the head and shaft of a simple nail, a shape later borrowed for other meanings.

example.hanzi: 他最喜欢吃巧克力布丁。
example.pinyin: tā zuì xǐhuān chī qiǎokèlì bùdīng.
example.english: He loves eating chocolate pudding most of all.
example.fact: The word pudding originally referred to savory dishes, like sausage encased in an animal's stomach, in medieval England. Sweet, dessert-style puddings only became the dominant meaning of the word in the 18th and 19th centuries.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
口 (mouth) — 喊 describes an action made with the mouth, shouting.
咸 (xián) gives a sound distantly related to hǎn, having drifted apart over time.
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
口 (mouth) — relates directly to 叫's meaning 'to call out, shout; to be named.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from jiào.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在操场上大喊大叫地跑来跑去。
example.pinyin: háizimen zài cāochǎng shàng dàhǎndàjiào de pǎo lái pǎo qù.
example.english: The children ran around the playground shouting and screaming.
example.fact: The Guinness World Record for the loudest human scream is held by Jill Drake of the UK, who reached 129 decibels in 2023 — roughly comparable to standing near a jet engine at takeoff.

components.note: Stone — magnetism was first discovered in a type of stone.
Gives the sound zī, related to cí but drifted apart over time.
巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'

example.hanzi: 这些老歌都保存在磁带里。
example.pinyin: zhèxiē lǎo gē dōu bǎocún zài cídài lǐ.
example.english: These old songs are all stored on cassette tape.
example.fact: Magnetic tape recording was pioneered in Germany in the 1930s with the Magnetophon. The format later became the backbone of both music cassettes and, for decades, the primary medium for storing digital computer data before affordable hard drives took over.

components.note: ⺊ (a divination crack/omen) — a sign to be interpreted
口 (mouth) — speaking the meaning of the omen aloud
扌 (hand) — relates to 据's meaning 'to rely on, according to,' as if grasping evidence in hand.
居 (jū) gave the base sound; the pronunciation later shifted to jù, keeping the same final but a different tone.

example.hanzi: 智能手机占据了我们大部分的空闲时间。
example.pinyin: zhìnéng shǒujī zhànjù le wǒmen dàbùfèn de kòngxián shíjiān.
example.english: Smartphones occupy most of our free time.
example.fact: Global surveys report that the average smartphone user now spends over four hours a day on their device, a figure that has roughly doubled over the past decade as mobile internet access and app usage have expanded.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — a heavy, ripe stalk of grain standing steady in the field ties to 稳's meaning 'stable, steady.'
㥯 (wěn) gives the sound — an exact match with 稳's reading wěn.
亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'

example.hanzi: 大家保持冷静，先稳住局势。
example.pinyin: dàjiā bǎochí lěngjìng, xiān wěnzhù júshì.
example.english: Everyone stay calm, let's stabilize the situation first.
example.fact: Modern rockets and satellites use spinning gyroscopes or reaction wheels to stay stable in orientation. The same principle keeps a spinning bicycle wheel resistant to tipping over, a phenomenon studied in physics since the 19th century.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 丝 is a simplified picture of two twisted strands of silk thread.
毛 (hair) — 毫 originally meant a fine, thin hair.

example.hanzi: 他丝毫没有感到害怕。
example.pinyin: tā sīháo méiyǒu gǎndào hàipà.
example.english: He didn't feel afraid in the slightest.
example.fact: The gravitational-wave detector LIGO can measure distance changes smaller than one ten-thousandth the width of a proton. That almost unimaginably tiny precision let scientists confirm ripples in spacetime that Einstein had predicted a century earlier.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 综 originally described the heddle threads on a loom, extending to 'weave together, combine.'
宗 (zōng) gives the sound — an exact match with 综.
人, shaped here like a lid, sits atop the character.
口 (mouth, or a container's opening) — a lid closing over an opening gave 合 its meaning 'to close, to fit together, to combine.'
疒 (sickness) — 症 names a symptom or disease.
正 (zhèng) is an exact match for the sound of 症.

example.hanzi: 医生诊断他患有代谢综合症。
example.pinyin: yīshēng zhěnduàn tā huàn yǒu dàixiè zōnghézhèng.
example.english: The doctor diagnosed him with metabolic syndrome.
example.fact: The term Stockholm syndrome was coined after a 1973 bank robbery in Stockholm, Sweden, during which hostages held for six days developed sympathetic feelings toward their captors. Criminologists have since studied the same response in other hostage situations.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 格 originally meant a wooden branch or standard, extended to 'pattern, style, rule.'
各 (gè) gives a sound hint — 格 is pronounced gé, sharing the same rhyme with a different tone.
木 (tree), doubled — two trees side by side depict a cluster of trees, the source of 林's meaning 'forest, grove.'

example.hanzi: 格林先生是这所学校的校长。
example.pinyin: Gélín xiānsheng shì zhè suǒ xuéxiào de xiàozhǎng.
example.english: Mr. Green is the principal of this school.
example.fact: Green is among the ten most common surnames in England, originally an occupational or descriptive nickname for someone who lived near a village green or who often wore green clothing in the Middle Ages.

components.note: 火 (fire) — smoke, 烟's meaning, rises from fire.
因 (yīn) gives a rhyme close to yān, with the tone shifted.
雨 (rain) shows 雾 relates to weather.
务 (wù) gives the exact sound of 雾.

example.hanzi: 浓浓的烟雾笼罩着整个城市。
example.pinyin: nóngnóng de yānwù lóngzhào zhe zhěnggè chéngshì.
example.english: Thick smog blanketed the entire city.
example.fact: The Great Smog of London in December 1952 trapped a thick layer of coal-smoke pollution over the city for five days and is estimated to have caused several thousand deaths. It directly led to the UK's Clean Air Act of 1956.

components.note: Mountain — original sense of a small hill or mound.
Gives the sound gāng, related to gǎng but drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.

example.hanzi: 每个员工都要坚守自己的岗位。
example.pinyin: měi ge yuángōng dōu yào jiānshǒu zìjǐ de gǎngwèi.
example.english: Every employee must stay firm at their post.
example.fact: Before automation, lighthouse keepers held one of the most isolated jobs in the world, sometimes staying at remote posts for months at a time to keep the light burning. Most countries had fully automated their lighthouses by the late 20th century.

components.note: 止 (a foot) sits above the rest of the character, showing forward movement.
舟 (a boat) — a foot stepping onto a boat suggested moving ahead, giving 前 its meaning 'front, before, forward.'
扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 诚实是建立信任的前提。
example.pinyin: chéngshí shì jiànlì xìnrèn de qiántí.
example.english: Honesty is the precondition for building trust.
example.fact: Euclid's Elements, written around 300 BC, built the entire foundation of geometry from just five basic premises, or axioms. That method of reasoning from a small set of assumptions to derive complex results became a model for mathematics and logic for over two thousand years.

components.note: Sun — warmth comes from the sun.
Gives the sound yuán, related to nuǎn but drifted apart over time.
口 (mouth) — ties to harmony as speaking together in accord
禾 (hé, grain) gives the sound — matches 和's pronunciation hé

example.hanzi: 今天太阳出来了，暖和多了。
example.pinyin: jīntiān tàiyáng chūlái le, nuǎnhuo duō le.
example.english: The sun came out today, so it's much warmer.
example.fact: Iceland heats roughly 90% of its homes using geothermal energy piped directly from underground hot springs, taking advantage of the same volcanic activity that produces the country's famous outdoor thermal pools.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
旦 (dàn) gives the sound — 但 is also pronounced dàn, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 他不但聪明，而且非常勤奋。
example.pinyin: tā bùdàn cōngming, érqiě fēicháng qínfèn.
example.english: He is not only smart, but also very hardworking.
example.fact: Marie Curie is not only the first woman to win a Nobel Prize but also the only person in history to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences — physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911.

components.note: 米 (grain) — 粉 names a fine powder, originally made by grinding grain.
分 (fēn) gives a sound very close to fěn, sharing the initial and rhyme — only the tone differs.
纟 (silk/thread) — 红 originally described a color of dyed silk, hence 'red'
工 (gōng) gives a loose sound connection to 红's reading hóng

example.hanzi: 她穿着一条粉红色的裙子。
example.pinyin: tā chuānzhe yì tiáo fěnhóngsè de qúnzi.
example.english: She was wearing a pink skirt.
example.fact: Flamingos are born with gray feathers and only turn pink because of pigments called carotenoids in the algae and crustaceans they eat. Flamingos raised on a diet lacking these pigments, as in some zoos, can remain pale or white.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迷 originally described losing one's way while walking, extending to 'confused, obsessed.'
米 (mǐ) gives a sound distantly related to mí, having drifted apart over time.
心 (heart) — 恋 describes a heart drawn to and longing for someone or something.
亦 (yì) is only distantly related in sound to liàn — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.

example.hanzi: 他从小就迷恋赛车运动。
example.pinyin: tā cóngxiǎo jiù míliàn sàichē yùndòng.
example.english: He has been infatuated with car racing since childhood.
example.fact: During the Dutch 'tulip mania' of the 1630s, buyers became so infatuated with rare tulip bulbs that a single bulb could sell for more than a skilled craftsman earned in a decade — before the market collapsed almost overnight in 1637.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 信 relates to a person's word being trustworthy.
言 (speech, words) — a person standing behind their own words gave 信 its meaning 'to trust, believe; a letter.'
彳 pictures a person's legs walking.
走 (to walk/run) reinforces the idea of movement, giving 徒 its meanings 'on foot' and 'a follower who walks in someone's footsteps.'

example.hanzi: 很多信徒每年都会去麦加朝圣。
example.pinyin: hěn duō xìntú měi nián dōu huì qù Màijiā cháoshèng.
example.english: Many believers make the pilgrimage to Mecca every year.
example.fact: The annual Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca draws roughly two million Muslim believers from around the world each year, making it one of the largest peaceful gatherings of people on Earth.

components.note: 一 (a line, representing a target or standard) — 正 shows a foot arriving exactly at the right mark.
止 (foot, to stop) — arriving and stopping precisely at the target gives 正 its meaning of 'correct' or 'straight.'
事 originally pictured a hand holding a forked hunting or recording instrument, associated with carrying out official duties — the source of its meaning 'affair, matter, to serve.'

example.hanzi: 别闲聊了，咱们说点正事。
example.pinyin: bié xiánliáo le, zánmen shuō diǎn zhèngshì.
example.english: Stop chit-chatting, let's talk about something important.
example.fact: The Pomodoro Technique, developed in the late 1980s by Francesco Cirillo, uses a kitchen timer shaped like a tomato (pomodoro in Italian) to break work into focused 25-minute intervals — a simple method still widely used today to stay on task.

components.note: Eye radical at the bottom of the older form, thought to derive from a component meaning 'to watch/examine,' unrelated in meaning to the modern anatomical sense of 睾.
九, used here purely for its curled shape rather than its meaning 'nine,' pictures a hand or fist.
丶 represents a small round object, like a pebble or pill, held within the fist.

example.hanzi: 这项检查是为了排查睾丸方面的疾病。
example.pinyin: zhè xiàng jiǎnchá shì wèile páichá gāowán fāngmiàn de jíbìng.
example.english: This exam is meant to screen for testicular conditions.
example.fact: Human testes hang outside the body cavity because sperm production requires a temperature slightly cooler than the core body temperature, roughly 2 to 4 degrees Celsius lower. Muscles in the scrotum draw the testes closer to or farther from the body to regulate this temperature.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching to take hold of something.
耳 (ear) — from an ancient battlefield practice of taking a fallen enemy's ear as proof of a kill, the origin of 取's meaning 'to take, obtain.'
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'

example.hanzi: 医生小心地把弹片从伤口里取出。
example.pinyin: yīshēng xiǎoxīn de bǎ dànpiàn cóng shāngkǒu lǐ qǔchū.
example.english: The doctor carefully removed the shrapnel from the wound.
example.fact: The world's first cash-dispensing ATM was installed by Barclays Bank in London in 1967. The inventor reportedly tested it with a cheque cashed for a fictional sum, and the machine could dispense at most £10 per transaction.

components.note: 分 (to divide, distribute) shows the act of handing something out.
页 (a page or document) suggests a certificate or notice being given out.
大 (big) — 奖 describes something given as a big reward.
丬 (qiáng) gives a sound close to jiǎng.

example.hanzi: 颁奖仪式将在下周举行。
example.pinyin: bānjiǎng yíshì jiāng zài xià zhōu jǔxíng.
example.english: The award ceremony will be held next week.
example.fact: The Academy Award statuette, nicknamed 'Oscar,' is made of gold-plated britannium and stands 13.5 inches tall. The earliest statuettes, first awarded in 1929, were solid bronze and only gold-plated from the 1930s onward.

meanings: variant of 答覆|答复[da2 fu4]

components.note: 竹 (bamboo) — ancient answers were sometimes recorded on bamboo slips.
合 is close in sound to 答's reading dá, and its meaning 'to fit together' reinforces the idea of a response matching a question.
亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'

example.hanzi: 公司已经对客户的投诉做出了答复。
example.pinyin: gōngsī yǐjīng duì kèhù de tóusù zuò chū le dáfù.
example.english: The company has already responded to the customer's complaint.
example.fact: In 2018, a message in a bottle thrown from a German research ship in 1886 was found on an Australian beach, still carrying its original reply card. At 132 years, it became the oldest message in a bottle ever recovered — finally answered more than a century later.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 诡 relates to deceptive words or schemes.
危 (wēi) gives a sound distantly related to guǐ, having drifted apart over time.
讠 (speech) — 计 relates to counting or planning through words and numbers.
十 (shí) gives a hint of the sound — 计 is pronounced jì, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 敌人的诡计被我们及时发现了。
example.pinyin: dírén de guǐjì bèi wǒmen jíshí fāxiàn le.
example.english: We discovered the enemy's trick in time.
example.fact: The legendary Trojan Horse, described in Homer's Iliad and Virgil's Aeneid, tells of Greek soldiers hiding inside a giant wooden horse to trick their way into the city of Troy. The story is the origin of the modern term 'Trojan horse' used for deceptive computer malware.

components.note: 虍 (a tiger's stripes, the tiger radical) evokes the awe and reverence one might feel before a powerful tiger.
The lower portion originally depicted a kneeling or bowing figure, reinforcing the sense of respectful submission that gave 虔 its meaning 'reverent, pious, devout.'
讠 (speech) — 诚 relates to speaking honestly and sincerely.
成 (chéng) gives the sound — an exact match with 诚's reading chéng.

example.hanzi: 他是一个非常虔诚的教徒。
example.pinyin: tā shì yí ge fēicháng qiánchéng de jiàotú.
example.english: He is a very devout believer.
example.fact: Mount Athos in Greece has been home to Eastern Orthodox monks for over a thousand years and remains one of the strictest religious communities in the world — women have been barred from setting foot on the peninsula since at least the 9th century.

components.note: A drawing of a tree trunk with branches spreading up and roots below.
亻 (person) — 偶 originally described a wooden figure or idol shaped like a person, later extending to 'a pair' and 'by chance.'
禺 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to 偶's reading ǒu, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这个木偶剧团来自捷克。
example.pinyin: zhège mù'ǒu jùtuán láizì Jiékè.
example.english: This puppet theater troupe is from the Czech Republic.
example.fact: Czech marionette puppetry is recognized by UNESCO as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The tradition dates back to the 19th century, when itinerant puppeteers performed folk tales and satire across Bohemia and Moravia.

components.note: 彡 (shān) is the historical phonetic component of 参; sound change over time has left little resemblance to the modern reading cān
贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赛 originally related to offering valuables, later coming to mean 'to compete.'
宀 (mián) gives a sound distantly related to sài, having drifted apart over time.

者's ancient form is thought to have depicted plants or a bundle of firewood being sorted; over time the original picture faded and the character was repurposed as a suffix meaning 'the one who...' or 'a person of a certain kind.'

example.hanzi: 这次比赛共有五百名参赛者。
example.pinyin: zhè cì bǐsài gòng yǒu wǔbǎi míng cānsàizhě.
example.english: There are five hundred competitors in this competition in total.
example.fact: The New York City Marathon is one of the largest marathons in the world, with roughly 50,000 official finishers each year — more people than live in many small towns, all crossing the same finish line in Central Park.
